summary.oneLiner: Vidhi delivered resilient FY26 results with flat revenue but expanded EBITDA margins to 20.5% via mix optimization, while guiding for a structural shift toward high-margin pharma coatings (CoatIcon) and new specialty lines requiring ~INR85cr capex over 18 months. The thesis hinges on successful commercialization of CoatIcon by mid-FY28 and recovery in emerging markets post-geopolitical stabilization.

one-line thesis: Vidhi delivered resilient FY26 results with flat revenue but expanded EBITDA margins to 20.5% via mix optimization, while guiding for a structural shift toward high-margin pharma coatings (CoatIcon) and new specialty lines requiring ~INR85cr capex over 18 months. The thesis hinges on successful commercialization of CoatIcon by mid-FY28 and recovery in emerging markets post-geopolitical stabilization.
financial scorecard: Revenue INR380cr (-0.6% YoY); EBITDA INR78cr (+14.7% YoY), Margin 20.52% (vs 17.91%); PAT INR49.15cr (+10.8% YoY); Order Book: Not disclosed (project-based sampling); Net Debt: Negligible (D/E 0.28%). One-offs: Sharp rise in 'other expenses' due to front-loaded US FDA certification fees ($1/kg) and R&D costs, partially recoverable from customers.
guidance: Revenue: Full utilization of Dahej/Roha in FY27; Margin: Manufacturing margins ~24-25%, overall to rise with value-added mix; Order Inflow: CoatIcon in aggressive sampling (6-month approval cycle); Capex: INR5-12cr for CoatIcon scale-up + INR75-85cr for new specialty line in FY27, commissioning mid-FY28.
order book & pipeline: No traditional order book; CoatIcon range in aggressive sampling/qualification with multi-pharma clients globally; 6-month approval cycle cited.
segment / subsidiary detail: Manufacturing sales INR330cr (bulk of EBITDA); Value-added products currently 5% of mix, targeting 10-12% in FY27; US/North America exports ~19% (not 44% as rumored); Emerging markets (Iran, Bangladesh, Philippines) currently depressed but expected to rebound sharply.
growth verticals / optionality: CoatIcon tablet coating systems (pharma forward integration); New specialty chemical line (R&D/pilot stage) with thin competition; Doubling value-added product contribution in FY27.
margins & cost dynamics: Manufacturing EBITDA margin ~24-25%; Value-added products carry 'much above average' margins; Cost pressure from withdrawal of export finance subvention (Dec 2025) increased interest costs.
capex / expansion: INR5-12cr for CoatIcon; INR75-85cr for new specialty line (Phase 1); Total ~INR80-95cr primarily in FY27; 18-month timeline to commissioning.
capital allocation: Dividend cut to fund capex; Reinvestment into R&D (INR4.5-5cr in analytical equipment); 60+ dedicated chemists; Debt-free balance sheet supports aggressive deployment.
risks & watch-items: Geopolitical tensions impacting emerging markets (Middle East, SE Asia); US tariff volatility (though stabilizing); Regulatory speculation on synthetic dyes (management dismisses ban rumors); Customer inventory destocking lag.
management quality / tone: Confident on long-term transformation; Defensive on short-term macro headwinds; Aggressive on R&D pipeline; Dismissive of synthetic dye ban rumors as 'false perception'.
non-obvious takeaways: Management clarified US export share is only 19% (not 44%), reducing perceived regulatory risk; Inventory levels at customer end were down 50% during tariff panic, implying potential replenishment cycle; FDA certification costs are pass-through but hit P&L timing in Q4.

themes.title: Import-substitution / China+1 specialty chemicals
themes.need: After the worst agrochem/chemicals year in living memory, the cycle is turning on China+1 reshoring and global pigment/dye consolidation. SUDARSCHEM is now #2 global pigment player post-Heubach; SUMICHEM posted record FY26 margins; AETHER/ANURAS/DEEPAKNTR/CLEAN add CRAMS + backward-integration; war-driven RM/freight inflation is being passed through. Q1FY27 shows the reshoring build-out actually landing: HSCL grew consolidated revenue 28% to INR 1,432cr with PAT INR 228cr (+27%) at a 22% EBITDA margin while opening three new value ladders in a single quarter (carbon nanotube 200 MTPA by Q4FY27, super-speciality carbon black 6,000 MTPA by FY28, and India's first commercial anthraquinone/carbazole plant), all self-funded with no incremental debt; TATVA grew revenue 43% YoY and delivered its first commercial-plant-scale semiconductor batch, qualified by the customer and called 'the glaring achievement of the past decade' (though commercialisation is explicitly not before Q4 CY2028); FCL tripled total income to INR 386.72cr (+165%) with Texas capacity nearly doubled to 148,000 MTPA and already running 63% on a single shift, so its next revenue leg needs only USD 1-2mn of capex.
themes.driver: Volume rebound as destocking ends; price hikes sticking; new value-ladder commissioning (HSCL CNT/carbon black) and semiconductor-materials qualification (TATVA).
